# Summary


**Background**:
Volatile anaesthetics contribute substantially to the environmental footprint of operating rooms.
CONTRAfluran^TM^ (ZeoSys Medical GmbH, Berlin, Germany)
passively captures sevoflurane at the anaesthesia machine exhaust port
for subsequent thermal desorption and pharmaceutical reuse.
Multicentre evidence on capture efficiency under routine clinical conditions is lacking.

**Methods**:
In this prospective, multicentre, international observational study conducted from
`r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[1L], "month"), "%B %Y")`
to
`r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[2L], "month"), "%B %Y")`
across `r n_center["initial"]` hospitals in Germany and Austria,
`r n_agcs["initial"]` CONTRAfluran canisters were deployed across
`r n_ors["initial"]` operating rooms,
each supplied with `r n_bottles_per_or` standardised sevoflurane bottles
(`r sevo_bottle_ml` mL, `r sevo_g_per_bottle` g each).
Case-level data were collected prospectively by the attending anaesthesiologist
using paper-based case report forms.
After exclusion of canisters with insufficient documentation,
fewer than ten cases, loss at ZeoSys,
or outlier status determined by cluster analysis,
`r n_agcs["final"]` canisters were submitted for batch thermal desorption.
Capture efficiency was defined as the ratio of recovered to administered sevoflurane.
Potential clinical predictors of per-canister recapture were explored
using LASSO regression with repeated cross-validation.

**Results**:
The `r n_agcs["final"]` analysed canisters were drawn from
`r n_ors["final"]` operating rooms across `r n_center["final"]` hospitals,
covering `r n_cases["final"]` of the `r n_cases["initial"]` documented anaesthesia cases.
ZeoSys recovered `r zeosys_sevo_weight_kg` kg
(`r zeosys_sevo_volume_l` L) of sevoflurane
at a purity exceeding `r zeosys_purity_pct`%,
corresponding to a capture efficiency of `r round(recovery_pct_final, 1)`%
relative to the `r n_agcs["final"]` analysed canisters
and `r round(recovery_pct_total, 1)`% relative to all `r n_agcs["initial"]` deployed canisters.
In an exploratory LASSO analysis,
the median fresh gas flow and the number of inhaled anaesthesia cases
were the main candidate predictors of per-canister recapture;
all predictors specific to total intravenous anaesthesia were eliminated.
Water trap use was independently associated with higher capture.
Stability selection corroborated only the dominant flow signal,
underscoring that the remaining associations require confirmation in larger samples.

**Conclusions**:
CONTRAfluran canisters recaptured approximately
`r round(recovery_pct_final, 0)`%
of administered sevoflurane under routine multicentre clinical conditions,
consistent with prior single-centre findings.
Fresh gas flow and the number of inhaled anaesthesia cases
were the main candidate predictors of per-canister recapture,
supporting targeted deployment in operating rooms
with a high proportion of inhaled anaesthesia.

**Keywords**:
inhaled anaesthesia; sevoflurane; vapour capture technology; capture efficiency;
